Proof-level rigor across 65 subjects + 258 prove-it deliverables ([BUILD]/[SOLVE]/[MEASURE]/[PROVE]/[ANALYZE]) + a parallel competitive-programming track. Ordered as a prerequisite DAG (Phase 0 → 5), not subject-by-subject. Every node = one atomic concept with a source pointer and ← requires / → enables links. Each section header carries the single best lecturer/course beyond the textbook + the assignment set to actually produce work. Multi-year; not a race.

Same token on each device → same progress everywhere. Lost a device? Revoke the token in GitHub settings; its blast radius is limited to your gists.

Links are canonical pointers chosen for stability: MIT OpenCourseWare course pages (with course numbers + assignment tabs), cp-algorithms.com per-algorithm pages, course homepages, and named textbook section/theorem references. Not every URL was individually live-checked; the named course + section still locates the material if a link moves. Nothing fabricated.
Build track (do, don't just read) — the forcing function a reading list lacks:
1. Nand2Tetris — build a working computer from NAND gates → CPU → assembler → VM → OS → compiler.
2. CMU 15-213 CSAPP labs — bomb, attack, cache, malloc, shell. Reading H&P ≠ building a memory system.
3. Onur Mutlu DDCA / 18-447 labs — pipelined → out-of-order core, cache & DRAM simulators. (Your day job, leveled up.)
Pair these with the architecture, OS, and PL sections below.
How to follow this plan (read first — 60 seconds):
1. The 23 threads below are your study order. The PHASE 0–5 sections further down are only the reference library — never study them top-to-bottom.
2. One-time: click "finished 6.042 — credit its 64 nodes" in the Today's-session box. Those concepts get ticked everywhere.
3. Daily: use the Today's session box. Pick the thread your roadmap year points at, keep 6 items. It only ever shows items whose prerequisites you've already ticked — do them in the shown order, each links its exact source (lecture / chapter / problem set).
4. Tick the checkbox when done (in the session list, a thread list, or a reference section — all the same checkbox). Progress saves automatically.
5. Weekly: do one [BUILD]/[SOLVE]/[MEASURE]/[PROVE] node — the prove-it deliverable at the end of whatever section you're inside. This is the anti-forgetting machinery; skipping it turns the plan back into a reading list.
6. The roadmap box under this one maps years → threads: 2026–27 = threads 01–04 spines, 2027–28 = finish 02 + 04 spines, and so on. Switch the thread selector as the roadmap advances — not before.
Why the roadmap mentions "Phase 0–2 cores": the first threads deliberately interleave that math with the systems nodes that consume it (thread 02 runs logic → ε–δ → ODEs → complex numbers → assembly → circuits → Verilog). You never do "a year of math" — you do math the day before it's needed.
Career roadmap (born 2001-04-13; plan starts 2026 at 25 — target: HFT or senior performance/chip-architect by 30–32):
2026–27 (25→26): Phase 0–2 cores + threads 01–04 spines begin. Ship the forcing functions: CS:APP data/bomb/malloc labs, 5-stage RV32I in Verilog (riscv-formal clean), Nand2Tetris. CP parallel track daily (cf_found → cf_ds).
2027–28 (26→27): Silicon thread spine: STA → CDC → FPGA timing-closure grind → PCIe/DMA. Nanosoft spine: zero-copy → io_uring → lock-free MPMC → xv6 labs → DPDK echo vs kernel baseline. Roofline + cache staircase measured. First role pivot: performance engineer / FPGA engineer / low-latency dev.
2028–29 (27→28): Depth that separates seniors: DRAM controllers/HBM/CXL, SerDes/FEC, PTP hardware timestamping demo, FPGA NIC (Corundum), mitigation-cost literacy (KPTI/retpolines). Start hft section + net_hft depth; CP to consistent Div-2 C solves.
2029–31 (28→30): Interview season (swe sw_interview + hft_hiring): FPGA dev / low-latency dev at an HFT, or perf/architecture team at a silicon company. Keep stochcalc + stats2_changepoint for quant-adjacent optionality.
2031–33 (30→32): Senior scope: own an architecture (memory hierarchy, NIC offload, or matching-engine adjacent), mentor, publish/measure. VLSI/tapeout (tinytapeout → OpenLane) if the chip-architect path wins.
Rule that makes this work: every [BUILD]/[SOLVE]/[MEASURE]/[PROVE] node is a deliverable with a definition of done — schedule one per week alongside concept nodes, or the concepts evaporate.

THE TRACK — 23 threads that cut across every subject

Subject boundaries are an administrative artifact, and keeping them as the study order is what stops you seeing that the material is one thing. The 65 sections further down stay as the reference substrate — where a concept lives and what it requires. These 23 threads are the study order. Each follows a single idea through every subject it appears in and ends in something you ship. A thread's list is the complete prerequisite closure of its payoff, ordered prerequisites-first: when you reach any item, this plan has already taught you everything it depends on. The subject tag on the right is deliberate — a normal session runs Rudin → Strang → Herlihy, and the point is that those are one argument in three costumes.

    19 · Analytic Continuation & the Complex Plane 0/104

    Holomorphy is a rigidity condition so strong that local data determines global behaviour. Residues then trivialize integrals you couldn't do.
    Ship this: Evaluate a family of real integrals by contour methods, implement a numerical inverse Laplace via residues, and map the zeta functional equation.
